correctness.rationale: Every paired-dominating set is total dominating and even, so the published equality gamma_t=q gives the lower bound. The published q-vertex total-dominating set supported in one coordinate is a clique because every pair has zero sum in another coordinate. It therefore has a perfect matching for even q; for odd q, adjoining a vertex with a nonzero second coordinate adjacent to zero gives a perfect matching on q+1 vertices. Fresh direct enumeration on F2xF2, F3xF3 and F3xF5 agrees.

originality.rationale: Shariatinia–Maimani–Yassemi already prove that the total-domination number of a finite reduced nonfield product is the smallest field size q and, in the proof, explicitly use S={(a,0,...,0):a in F1} as a q-vertex total-dominating set. Because there is a second factor, S is a clique: any two of its vertices have zero sum in that second coordinate. The audited paired-domination formula is therefore the immediate parity consequence of a published optimum clique witness: S itself has a perfect matching when q is even, and when q is odd one extra vertex adjacent to one member yields size q+1. Under the audit rule that direct corollaries are covered even without identical wording, originality fails.
